title: The King's Twelve-Check Puzzle
body: During the Middle Ages, chess players loved solving complex puzzles called divided games. One grand challenge recorded for a Spanish king featured twenty-nine pieces crowded onto the board. To win, the black pieces had to deliver twelve consecutive checks in a row using only a single rook.

variants.lucy: Long ago in medieval Spain, a wise king named Alfonso loved to study beautiful chess puzzles. One of these ancient mind-teasers was packed with twenty-nine wooden pieces, filling almost every square on the board. It looked like a quiet, crowded forest waiting for a spark of magic.
variants.luca: To solve this ultimate challenge, the black side had to launch a daring, non-stop attack. A single, brave rook had to charge across the board and put the enemy king in danger twelve times in a row without stopping. One wrong move would ruin the whole mission, but a perfect run meant total victory.
variants.cn: 很久很久以前，在中世纪的西班牙，有一位聪明的国王，名叫阿方索。他最喜欢研究漂亮的国际象棋谜题啦。其中有一道古老的谜题，棋盘上密密麻麻摆了二十九个木头棋子，几乎把每个格子都占满了。看上去就像一片安安静静、挤挤挨挨的小森林，正等着一点魔法的火花呢。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
